acceptance_predicates.description: Every default human response begins with a clear sentence saying what the current command succeeded or failed to do, without requiring knowledge of internal status fields.
Default output contains only command-relevant facts and suppresses schema, transport, classification, empty, duplicate, and development-state metadata unless it changes the user's decision.
When user action is required, output ends with one clear next step and a valid copyable safe ASB command; terminal outcomes do not fabricate a next action.
Failures explain the human cause, distinguish user correction, host limitation, dependency unavailability, and product failure, preserve exit semantics, and say whether relevant state changed.
Every public ASB command and typed outcome has an explicit presentation; CI fails instead of falling back to a recursive JSON key/value dump when the command surface grows.
Explicit --json and --format json retain their schemas, semantics, exit codes, redaction, and stdout/stderr contracts.
A clean-install setup-to-plan-to-run-to-report/compare journey and TUI lifecycle routing are self-explanatory step by step using only the displayed human output.

definition_of_done: Before/after fixtures demonstrate concise command-aware output for representative successes and failures across the complete public command inventory.
Golden, semantic, exhaustiveness, suggested-command, JSON compatibility, exit-code, privacy, redirection, NO_COLOR, terminal-width, and clean user-journey tests pass.
The exact signed+DCO candidate receives independent review, green exact-head CI, a signed reviewed-tree merge, green exact-main CI, and a privacy-safe acceptance receipt.

inputs.description: Existing ASB command result and error envelopes, exit codes, and remediation data.
The exact current-main public ASB commands, subcommands, documented journeys, and structured output contracts.

outputs.description: A command-aware presentation model and renderer with outcome, relevant facts, warnings, and optional next action.
Exhaustive fixtures and tests for public command and outcome variants.
Updated help and examples showing concise outcomes, safe next commands, JSON opt-in, and diagnostic-detail opt-in.

gates.description: Every public command and typed outcome maps to an explicit tested human presentation.
Displayed next commands are valid, safe, context-appropriate, and secret-free.
Machine-readable output, exit behavior, privacy, and command authority remain unchanged.
Independent review, exact-head CI, signed exact-tree integration, and exact-main CI all pass.
